title: Plan D: Cinematic AI Short Films (Agent Pipeline)
summary: Brief & deconstruct → multi-agent pipeline → character anchors → audio-first → animatic preview → shot generation → spec assembly + minimal repair + QC
scenario: Best for 5-15 minute narrative shorts, one-person AI film studios, and batch content production. Combines multi-agent orchestration, animatic-first iteration and triple QC gates — the most engineering-grade advanced route (inspired by OpenMontage, movie-gen and ViMax).

steps.title: Brief and reference deconstruction
steps.detail: Fix the platform, duration, style and budget cap up front. Study reference shorts (high engagement, similar length) and decompose their structure, shot count, transitions and sound design into a reference blueprint.
steps.tips: Set budget and acceptance criteria before starting, or the agent pipeline will burn money uncontrolled.

steps.title: Multi-agent orchestration
steps.detail: Orchestrate Writer → Director → Producer → QC agents: the Writer produces the script and 3-layer plan (event / scene / shot); the Director outputs the storyboard and multi-camera options; the Producer screens reference images and validates cross-shot consistency; QC generates parallel candidates and scores them with a VLM. Steal the architecture from open-source ViMax, storyforge or ArcReel.
steps.tips: Route creative decision points to you for approval — never let it 'wing it'. Bake in a budget cap and per-operation approval thresholds.

steps.title: Character anchors
steps.detail: Create canonical character look shots (Anchors) as cross-shot consistency references, then derive a first-frame image per scene from them. The first frame is the 'anchor' for each generation, setting physics and lighting.
steps.tips: Anchor sheets need front / side / back views on a plain background; every later shot references the same set.

steps.title: Audio-first across the whole film
steps.detail: Pick character voices, then produce the full voiceover, BGM and ambience for the entire film. Audio-first lets every frame lock to the soundtrack and enables the preview — professional long-form always puts sound before picture.
steps.tips: Tag emotions in the voiceover; keep voice, music and ambience as separate mix layers with independent control.

steps.title: Animatic preview
steps.detail: Assemble the whole film from storyboard stills + the full soundtrack to validate pacing, shot flow and total duration. Nearly free, this is where every pacing problem is resolved before the expensive generation phase.
steps.tips: Generate only after the preview passes — this single gate saves over half your API budget.

steps.title: Shot generation
steps.detail: Input = first frame + Anchors + voice reference. Prompt priority: composition → subject → camera move → overall mood. Cap concurrency; on failure fix the first frame and retry. For longer films use keyframe mode or first/last-frame chaining to avoid the 'stitched shorts' feel.
steps.tips: Generate multiple candidates per shot; log a manifest (prompt / seed / model version) for reproducibility and rollback.

steps.title: Spec assembly + minimal repair + QC
steps.detail: Drive assembly from a timeline spec (film_spec: cuts / music spans / ambience / color / fades). Handle director notes with the cheapest fix: re-dub one line with a dub tool, re-render only one shot, catch mis-cast voices with an F0 pitch check. Triple QC gates: ASR back-check ≥0.85, CLIP consistency, ffprobe final review.
steps.tips: Keep intermediates (storyboard / voice samples / manifest) for regression; render with resume support so an interruption never loses progress.

pitfalls.title: Budget blowout
pitfalls.detail: Iterate free on the Animatic first; run cost estimates, spend caps and per-operation approvals before executing. Never let agents retry without limit.

pitfalls.title: Agents running wild
pitfalls.detail: Route key creative decisions to human approval and give agents a full SKILL/process doc — otherwise they skip the standard pipeline and invent worse flows.

pitfalls.title: Long-form feels stitched together
pitfalls.detail: Use keyframe mode / first-last-frame chaining instead of hard-stitching shorts; seamless straight cuts with continuous camera motion across shots.

pitfalls.title: Audio-video drift
pitfalls.detail: Audio-first + lip-sync audio prep spec (mono, trimmed silence, -3dB) + minimal repair (re-dub one line instead of re-rendering).

pitfalls.title: Consistency collapse
pitfalls.detail: Anchors + first/last-frame locking + VLM cross-shot checks. Don't rely on 'praying the same model remembers the character'.
